absent: Filesystem-specific initialization and release behavior behind configuration callbacks.
Complete layouts of configuration, parameter specification and parse-result records.
Lifetime and ownership transfer rules for configuration logs across handles.
Shutdown ordering that coordinates pending-error references with superblock activity.
Full path-resolution, mount-topology and permission checks beyond the block-device test.
Identity-mapping tables behind user-namespace ownership validation.
Progress guarantees for pin termination invoked from group cleanup.
Numeric values of directory-entry and internal file-type enumerations.

findings.text: Provides a reset operation for a filesystem configuration context that releases option ownership and restores neutral defaults suitable for reconfiguration.

Reconfiguration progresses through awaiting, parameter collection and failure stages with a dedicated purpose marker; cleaning establishes awaiting while finalization initializes only from that stage and then advances or records failure.
Exposes conversions between internal file classification, directory entry encoding and mode-derived values with a safe unknown result for out-of-range inputs.
Mode-derived table indexing masks the type portion of a mode and shifts it by a fixed displacement.

Exposes generic parameter parsing that resolves a key against a specification, reports deprecated use, checks flag polarity and delegates value handling to a type routine, returning a selector or a negative reason.

Key matching prefers entries whose flag nature aligns with the supplied value while keeping a same-name mismatch as fallback, with narrow support for a negated spelling only when the specification allows it.

Offers path lookup for parameters given as strings or filenames using caller-supplied resolution controls, optionally enforcing a block-device requirement and recording failures in the configuration log.

Kernel filename handling enforces a length ceiling, keeps short names inline with heap fallback for longer ones, starts with single ownership and audit capture, and frees according to remaining references.
Filename release tolerates absent or error values, guards against unbalanced accounting and separates shared-reference decrement from exclusive teardown.

Supplies validators that interpret textual or descriptor-based parameter values as booleans, integers of several widths and signs, enumerations, strings, descriptors and ownership identifiers, allowing emptiness only when specified.
Boolean acceptance covers numeric zero and one plus familiar affirmative and negative words mapped to logical outcomes.
Ownership conversion first obtains an unsigned value and then maps it within the caller identity scope, rejecting unrepresentable results.
Pin membership in superblock and mount collections is serialized by a dedicated spinlock, with completion notification performed under a separate wait-queue lock after list detachment.

Pin management supports insertion into both collections, removal with completion signaling, and group cleanup that repeatedly handles the current head under read-side protection until the collection empties.
Per-task filesystem state protects root, working directory and usage count with a sequence lock held exclusively for mutation and consistently sampled for duplication or replacement.

Global root redirection scans all threads under task-list protection, bypasses kernel and exiting tasks, replaces only entries matching both mount and entry, and transfers references to preserve lifetime.
Filesystem state lifetime uses paired path references with count-based reclamation; duplication acquires fresh references and copies creation mask while detachment and process exit drop references.

Replacing current filesystem state swaps pointers under task and sequence protection and yields the prior object for disposal only when its last reference drops, with additional handling for the initial user process.
Initial filesystem state begins with single ownership, unlocked sequencing and a standard restrictive creation mask, alongside a publish-once global for the user-space init instance.
Early user-space setup derives the initial root from the topmost overmount, installs it as both root and working directory and publishes a held reference for later checks.
Default error-event pool capacity is 32 entries.

Error-event allocation is refused during teardown based on activity state and pending-reference liveness, otherwise provides a cleared work-initialized object; release returns it to the pool and wakes the final waiter.

Error submission checks same-filesystem association and signed-number convention, stabilizes inode ownership when present, defers delivery to workqueue context and emits a rate-limited loss notice when resources are unavailable.
Deferred error delivery acts only for active owners, reports through filesystem-specific and generic notification with a positive number, then drops inode and event holdings.
Configuration log retrieval serializes with a user-API mutex, obtains one message fitting the caller length, handles transferable ownership and copies out after releasing the lock.
Log queue semantics distinguish empty and oversized requests with distinct negative outcomes, clear consumed entries and ownership marks and move the tail forward.
Context file behavior offers read access to queued messages and release handling that detaches and drops the configuration reference.
Opening a filesystem configuration validates privilege and flags, resolves the named filesystem, creates a mount context in creation stage with a fresh log and returns an anonymous descriptor.
Mount authorization requires administrative capability in the identity scope that owns the caller mount namespace.
Error-subsystem startup establishes a preallocated pool for event objects during initialization.
Group pin cleanup depends on external progress that removes the acted-upon head, otherwise re-observation of the same head would repeat indefinitely.
Initial process creation mask is 0022.
